input.query: beaconing web protocol command and control exfiltration over C2 channel

input.hypothesis: Host ip_81ee53a5ea2a, under principal u_8202e08c4b52 (lmoia@corp.example), is running an automated non-browser client (curl, with a fake "corp-sync/1.4" comment string) that beacons to the newly-registered domain billingcenter.click at a jittered ~4–6 minute interval, polling /api/v1/collect with small GETs and periodically uploading 27–75 KB POST bodies. This is consistent with HTTP-based C2 with data staged out over the same channel, not with normal user browsing. The scattered signal.burst detections that opened the incident are low-value noise (bursts of 1–5 events against a median of 1), but the billingcenter.click traffic within the same window is a genuine concern.

narrative.claim: The incident's opening signals are signal.burst detections with counts of 1–5 events per 5-minute bucket against a median of 1 (z undefined/infinite, MAD=0) — statistically weak on their own and not by themselves evidence of attack.

Within the same window, principal u_8202e08c4b52 from src_ip ip_81ee53a5ea2a made a sustained series of requests to the newly-registered domain billingcenter.click (event_key tagged 'Newly Registered and Revived Domains'), all resolving to a single dst_ip ip_662d9b40ce1a, from 2026-02-23T16:19Z to 18:16Z.

The requests are machine-generated: every one carries a non-browser curl/8.7.1 user-agent, several with a masquerading comment string 'corp-sync/1.4', and none carry a referrer, all hitting the same URL path /api/v1/collect.

The request timing is regular with light jitter — roughly every 4 to 6 minutes across ~2 hours (16:19, 16:25, 16:31, 16:36, 16:41, 16:47, 16:53, 16:57, 17:03, 17:06, 17:11, 17:16 …) — a beaconing shape rather than human-driven browsing.

Interleaved with the small polling GETs are recurring POSTs with markedly asymmetric byte volumes — 39,610 / 75,144 / 26,917 / 61,427 / 70,013 / 42,459 / 72,242 bytes outbound against small responses — consistent with data upload over the C2 channel rather than API polling.

Total outbound volume for this principal in the incident window was 423,370 bytes against a baseline mean of 0; however n_baseline_windows = 0, so no z-score could be computed and the baseline comparison is weak supporting evidence only.

Benign explanations considered: the 'corp-sync/1.4' user-agent and the 'nightly status report' query string suggest a sanctioned sync/telemetry job. This is undercut by the destination being a newly-registered .click domain unrelated to any corporate service, the inconsistent user-agent (the same client alternates between plain curl/8.7.1 and the corp-sync variant on adjacent requests), and the sporadic large uploads that a status-report poller would not produce. Ownership of billingcenter.click and any change-management record for a sync job should be confirmed before final disposition.

mitre_techniques.name: Web Protocols
mitre_techniques.rationale: Periodic HTTP GET/POST requests to a single newly-registered domain at ~4–6 minute jittered intervals from a non-browser curl user-agent with no referrer — a polling C2 heartbeat shape (events 8374099–8374157).

mitre_techniques.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
mitre_techniques.rationale: The same beaconing sessions carry recurring POSTs of 27–75 KB outbound with small responses to the same destination, i.e. increased outbound volume on the existing C2 connections rather than a new destination (events 8374104, 8374110, 8374122, 8374142, 8374157).

mitre_techniques.name: Masquerading
mitre_techniques.rationale: The client alternates between plain curl/8.7.1 and 'curl/8.7.1 (compatible; corp-sync/1.4)', a fabricated corporate-sync identity intended to make the traffic look sanctioned (events 8374099, 8374101, 8374105).

recommended_actions.rationale: Newly-registered domain receiving beaconed requests and multi-tens-of-KB POST uploads from an internal host; blocking cuts the suspected C2/exfil channel with low business risk.
Sole destination IP behind billingcenter.click for all 24 observed requests; blocking prevents fallback via direct IP or a renamed domain.
Source host running the automated beaconing client; isolation preserves state for forensics and stops further uploads pending confirmation that this is not a sanctioned job.
Principal associated with the outbound uploads; credentials should be rotated if the host is confirmed compromised.

input.contradicting_evidence:
Strongest benign case: the traffic is a textbook scheduled-agent pattern, not an attacker's. The 24 requests to billingcenter.click follow a strictly deterministic 3-request cycle — corp-sync-tagged GET /api/v1/collect?q=status, plain-curl GET ?q=nightly+status+report, then plain-curl POST ?q=status — repeating eight times, every ~5 min from 16:19 to 18:16 (8374099, 8374101, 8374104, 8374105, 8374108, 8374110, 8374115, 8374116, 8374118, 8374127, 8374132, 8374136, 8374147, 8374149, 8374150, 8374154, 8374156, 8374157). That perfectly periodic, self-announcing, single-URL, all-200 shape is what a monitoring/telemetry uploader looks like; real C2 usually varies paths or shows failures. The "inconsistent user-agent" the Investigator calls masquerading is in fact perfectly consistent by request role (the corp-sync comment appears on exactly the first GET of each cycle, e.g. 8374099, 8374105, 8374115, 8374119, 8374127, 8374140, 8374147, 8374154), i.e. two different code paths in one tool, not sloppy attacker spoofing. POST sizes of 4–75 KB (8374136 = 4,004 bytes vs 8374110 = 75,144) are also plausible batched log/telemetry payloads, and the "0 baseline" claim (narrative step 6) rests on n_baseline_windows = 0, so there is literally no history to say this is anomalous. The only detector signals in the incident are signal.burst events with count 1–5 vs median 1, MAD 0, z undefined (55777, 55841, 55857) plus a graph.betweenness signal with confidence 0.0011 and z_score null (61188) — no calibrated detector actually fired on this traffic.

Why it fails: the destination is a newly-registered/revived .click domain (every event tagged "Newly Registered and Revived Domains", e.g. 8374099, 8374157) whose name — billingcenter.click — has no relationship to any monitoring or sync product, and it is contacted by exactly one internal host/principal. A sanctioned telemetry job would resolve to a vendor domain, appear across many hosts, and not be the only destination of its kind in scope. Bidirectional payloads (GET responses of 13,548 and 13,135 bytes in 8374101 and 8374115 against 1 KB requests) mean the endpoint is also pushing content back — task retrieval, not one-way status reporting. And an inbound 13 KB response to a "status" poll plus 27–75 KB outbound POSTs to a stranger domain is exactly the interactive C2 + staged upload shape.
input.notes: Agree with true_positive on the billingcenter.click activity; the burst signals that opened the incident (55777–55858) should be treated as noise and not cited as corroboration. Scope caveat: all 24 confirmed events are within a single ~2h window on 2026-02-23 from one principal/host to one dst_ip (ip_662d9b40ce1a); I found no evidence linking the other in-scope users (adevin, ajenks, ehoffman, jlipfert) to this channel, so the incident should not be described as multi-user. block_domain_at_proxy and block_dst_ip are well supported. isolate_host and force_credential_reset are defensible but I would gate them on a quick check of change-management/asset ownership for a "corp-sync" job on that host, since the periodicity is unusually clean; the domain block is non-destructive and buys that time.

mitre_techniques.rationale: Destination is a newly-registered/revived domain (all events tagged 'Newly Registered and Revived Domains'), a common infrastructure-freshness indicator for C2 rendezvous (events 8374099, 8374157). Lower-confidence mapping.

input.summary: Host ip_81ee53a5ea2a, acting as principal u_8202e08c4b52 (lmoia@corp.example), made 24 automated curl requests to the newly-registered domain billingcenter.click (single dst_ip ip_662d9b40ce1a) over a ~2h window on 2026-02-23, in a deterministic ~5-minute 3-request cycle against one URL path (/api/v1/collect), with sizeable inbound responses (~13 KB) and recurring 27-75 KB outbound POSTs. Within the same period, principal u_8202e08c4b52 from src_ip ip_81ee53a5ea2a made a sustained series of requests to the newly-registered domain billingcenter.click, all resolving to the single dst_ip ip_662d9b40ce1a, between 2026-02-23T16:19Z and 18:16Z.

The strongest benign reading — a sanctioned 'corp-sync' nightly telemetry job — is undercut by the destination being a newly-registered .click domain whose name (billingcenter.click) bears no relation to any monitoring or sync product, and by it being contacted by exactly one internal host/principal rather than a fleet.

input.contradicting_evidence: The Devil's Advocate's strongest point is that the traffic is a textbook scheduled-agent pattern rather than an attacker's: the 24 requests follow a strictly deterministic three-request cycle repeating eight times every ~5 minutes, always the same URL path, all successful, with the 'corp-sync/1.4' comment appearing on exactly the first GET of each cycle (8374099, 8374105, 8374115, 8374127, 8374140, 8374147, 8374154). That is two consistent code paths in one tool, not sloppy attacker spoofing, and POST sizes ranging from ~4 KB (8374136) to ~75 KB (8374110) are plausible batched telemetry. He also correctly notes that no calibrated detector actually fired on this channel — the incident rests on signal.burst noise (counts 1-5 vs median 1, MAD 0, z undefined) plus a graph signal at 0.0011 confidence — and that the '0 baseline' argument is vacuous because n_baseline_windows = 0. This does not change the disposition because the Devil's Advocate himself concedes true_positive on the decisive points that remain unexplained by the benign reading: a newly-registered .click domain with a billing-themed name unrelated to any sync/monitoring product, contacted by exactly one host, returning ~13 KB payloads to 'status' polls while receiving tens of KB of uploads. It does justify capping confidence at moderate and gating the host-level containment actions.

recommended_actions.rationale: Newly-registered, semantically unrelated domain receiving periodic beacons and tens-of-KB POST uploads from one internal host; non-destructive containment that cuts the suspected channel while ownership is verified.
Sole destination IP behind billingcenter.click for all 24 observed requests; blocking prevents direct-IP or renamed-domain fallback.

Host running the automated client with bidirectional payload exchange and staged uploads. Recommend gating on a quick change-management/asset-ownership check for a legitimate 'corp-sync' job, per the Devil's Advocate; the domain block buys that time.
Principal associated with the outbound uploads; rotate credentials if the host is confirmed compromised rather than running a sanctioned job.
